family.label: The Slim family trust
family.note: Slim Family's Family Trust (a Mexican trust holding B Shares for the benefit of members of the Slim Family)

largestHolders.name: Control Empresarial de Capitales (formerly Inversora Carso; may be deemed controlled by the Slim Family)

structure.note: Single series of B Shares; 60,195 million B Shares were outstanding on March 31, 2026. The 20-F says the Slim Family (Carlos Slim Helú with his sons, daughters and grandchildren) may be deemed to control the company through the Family Trust (29.5%), Control Empresarial de Capitales (18.1%) and direct holdings (22.9% for family members including Carlos Slim Helú's own 8.6%), and may be able to elect a majority of the board.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Source: 2025 annual report on Form 20-F (accession 0001140361-26-017486, filed April 28, 2026), read on EDGAR; financial statements are in thousands of Mexican pesos (IFRS), recorded here in billions of MXN with no FX conversion. The new-year ifrs-full facts are not yet in SEC companyfacts, so no xbrl objects are given. OWNERSHIP (as of March 31, 2026, percentages of the 60,195 million B Shares outstanding, per footnote 1; the 20-F does not say whether treasury shares are excluded): the 20-F lists three holders above 5%, all linked to the Slim Family: the Family Trust 29.5%, Control Empresarial de Capitales 18.1%, and Carlos Slim Helú 8.6% (5,200 million shares, unchanged; the percentages rose because the share count fell with buybacks). They are recorded as three non-overlapping figures: Carlos Slim's own 8.6% as the leader, the Family Trust as the family figure, and Control Empresarial de Capitales as a holder. The 20-F's 22.9% for direct holdings of all Slim Family members is NOT recorded because it includes Carlos Slim's 8.6% (overlap); it says no family member other than Carlos Slim Helú individually directly owns more than 5.0%. No all-inclusive family total is stated, and the figures were not summed. pctVoting is null because there is a single series with one vote per share. Relation 'founder' follows data.js; the 20-F does not use the word. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line 'Dividends paid' (Ps.33,159,586 thousand) does not separate dividends to non-controlling interests; the statement of changes in equity shows 2025 dividends declared of Ps.31,388,472 thousand to owners of the parent and Ps.2,196,223 thousand to non-controlling interests, and the MD&A says 'We paid Ps.33.2 billion in dividends in 2025'. No figure for dividends paid to the company's own shareholders alone is stated, so the cash line is used and labelled as total; nothing was subtracted. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line (Ps.11,944,156 thousand); the MD&A says the company spent Ps.11.9 billion repurchasing its own shares in the open market in 2025. STOCK COMP: null; the 20-F discloses no share-based compensation expense or employee share plan. GEOGRAPHY: external revenues (after removing intersegment revenues) by the company's reportable segments; they sum to consolidated total revenues. 'Uruguay, Paraguay and Chile' includes Claro Chile, consolidated after its acquisition (note 12 a).

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: income taxes paid as presented in operating activities of the cash-flow statement (thousands of Mexican pesos); the caption does not say whether refunds are netted. R&D not reported as a separate line in the FY2025 20-F. The new-year ifrs-full facts are not yet in SEC companyfacts, so no xbrl object is given.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (FY2025 Form 20-F). IFRS filer that classifies interest paid in financing, so it is added back (32,325,287); income taxes paid are in operating. Lease payments (51,585,889, "Payment of liability related to right-of-use of assets") are in financing. Interest expense on lease liabilities was 16,156,752 in 2025 (lease note), but the 20-F does not say whether the cash paid for it sits in "Interest paid" or in the right-of-use payment line, so nothing more is added; if it is in the latter, paidOut is understated by up to about 2%. Interest received (2,504,220) sits in operating; dividends received are in investing. The USD column in the 20-F is a convenience translation and is not used; FX: calendar-2025 average. The new-year ifrs-full facts are not yet in SEC companyfacts, so no xbrl objects are given.

marketcap.notes: One series of B Shares, priced from the primary listing on the Mexican Stock Exchange (AMXB.MX, MXN) rather than the NYSE ADSs (AMX, 20 B Shares each). The count is the third-quarter 2026 results' 'Shares Outstanding End of Period' of 59.7 billion at September 30, 2026, which is stated only to one decimal (so it is precise to about ±50 million shares). The FY2025 20-F gives an exact 60,195 million B Shares at March 31, 2026; the company has kept buying back shares since, so the newer, rounded figure is used.
